external_primary_crosschecks.note: Primary abstract confirms evaluation-meta-knowledge fine-tuning, six safety benchmarks, persistence without explicit verbalized evaluation awareness, and released code/models.
Primary abstract confirms Python PHR overestimate up to 9.4 pp, seven defenses across 8 models x 4 languages, RAG reductions in 18/32 cells, and adversarial PHR increases up to 45 pp.
Primary abstract confirms 2,823 episodes, AUROC 0.872, cold-vs-recalibrated transfer 0.527/0.885, 45% vs 16% recovery and 52%->73% task success.
Primary abstract confirms 14.6-20.4% token savings at 5% FPR and Qwen3.6-27B 66.6%->71.8% resolution at 25% FPR versus 66.8% cold restart.
Primary abstract confirms AUROC about 0.94 can coexist with up to ~26 pp degradation and that a 50-task pilot predicts intervention sign across tested settings.
Primary abstract confirms semantic rollback attack classes Action Replay and Authority Resurrection and proof-of-concept validation; defense is proposed.
Primary abstract confirms transactional progress-aware tool semantics and separation of fault recovery from externally visible effects.
Primary abstract confirms reversibility taxonomy, formal irreversibility limits and StreamBench validation of Revision Absorber.
Primary abstract confirms conditional e-values/e-processes under adaptive minimax updates with fresh randomness and adaptive switching.
Primary abstract confirms a per-generation sampling budget and Archive/Parallel-Adaptive/Deep-Grid methods for uncertain QD.
Primary abstract confirms six cloud-service categories, 9 production Skills, 98 references, +23.0 points over self-reflection and +15.4 over single-turn-QA evolution.
Primary abstract confirms step-level Shapley attribution with boundary-adaptive sampling on SkillsBench; detailed configuration counts remain unverified here.
Primary abstract confirms MindSkillEvolve improves SpreadsheetBench success by 9.2 pp; code-path admission semantics remain a separate artifact claim.

assessments.tested_scope: Inspected public DriftLens UC8 wrapper/entrypoint/window generator at author commit 0b7b943b128f8e23b56e5cd56fa40bc3dd35119e.
assessments.rationale: Direct code-path inspection identifies missing --run_driftlens, inert --seed and threshold_sensitivity handling, and a radius2 artifact-lineage mismatch; these are strong reproducibility-contract findings.
limits: Not evidence that the published paper used the broken wrapper unchanged.
Missing public radius2 generator is an artifact gap, not proof of nonexistence.
No independent numerical detector reproduction.

assessments.tested_scope: Composition of constrained policy-improvement, multi-objective SPIBB and anytime-valid off-policy inference under each source's assumptions.
assessments.rationale: Multiple primary sources directly support current-baseline expected-cost constraints, separate objective certificates and anytime-valid OPE; the exact automation gate is a synthesis rather than a single published theorem.
limits: Expected cumulative cost is not pathwise hard safety.
Adaptive candidate generation from the same evaluation stream needs separate selection-validity control.
Support/importance-weight failure can prevent useful certification.

assessments.tested_scope: Finite fixed policy class under logged contextual-bandit data, overlap and variance-growth conditions.
assessments.rationale: Primary 2026 theory gives time-uniform survivor-set guarantees and gap-dependent stopping with simulation savings; scope is unusually explicit.
limits: Does not validate arbitrary data-dependent candidate addition.
Poor overlap or exploding importance weights break usefulness.
No direct autonomous-agent deployment study.

assessments.tested_scope: One-sided sign-symmetry null, precommitted discordant horizon N, random total task cost.
assessments.rationale: Closed-form continuation and exact dynamic-program calculations provide an internally checkable martingale construction with finite-sample null size and power; classical exact-McNemar/inverse-sampling literature anchors the terminal test.
limits: Worker-local derivation and numerics are not independent replication.
Does not give fixed-total-task terminal equivalence.
Scope depends on conditional sign symmetry.

assessments.tested_scope: Fixed total task horizon; predictable discordance propensity; reference-rho terminal geometry used only to choose a sign bet.
assessments.rationale: One-step validity identity is analytically clean and the Monte Carlo comparison is substantial, but the projected policy and its power advantage are worker-local and not a published matched-pair method.
limits: Reference mismatch can reduce power.
Not terminal-equivalent to McNemar.
No independent rerun of the 600k-rep comparisons.

assessments.tested_scope: Outcome-adaptive predictable discordance rates under local sign symmetry; fixed total task horizon.
assessments.rationale: Exact control DP constructs Type-I inflation well above 0.05 while the sign e-process remains valid by conditional expectation, giving a sharp adaptive-evaluation failure mode.
limits: This is a worker-derived counterexample, not a direct empirical benchmark failure.
Does not challenge standard nonadaptive matched-pair McNemar guarantees.

assessments.tested_scope: Fine-tuning on evaluation-design meta-knowledge and measuring six safety benchmarks across tested model families; includes multi-seed Nemotron replication.
assessments.rationale: Primary study uses a direct causal training intervention, reports large harmful-benchmark refusal shifts with benign over-refusal tradeoff, and releases code/models; effects persist without explicit evaluation-awareness verbalization.
limits: Benchmark behavior is not deployment-continuous safety.
Higher refusal can partly reflect utility loss.
Does not imply all safety post-training gains are evaluation-meta-knowledge.

assessments.tested_scope: Seven inference-time defenses across 8 models x 4 languages under standard and fabricated-package prompts.
assessments.rationale: Primary source directly verifies a 9.4 pp Python bookkeeping overestimate, RAG reductions in 18/32 cells, up-to-45 pp adversarial PHR increase and threat-model-dependent defense ordering.
limits: Full per-cell table provenance was not reconstructed in this wave.
Headline 18/32 reductions do not say whether the remaining cells tie or worsen.
Independent replication is absent.

assessments.tested_scope: ADVERSA multi-turn pilot plus documented longer development runs; attacker trained single-turn and deployed up to 10 turns in main pilot.
assessments.rationale: Direct instrumentation shows attacker refusals suppress victim calls and longer preliminary runs drift away from the attack objective, establishing evaluator-attacker reliability as a measurement variable.
limits: Main pilot is only 15 conversations.
Longer drift evidence comes from development runs with different prompting.
Does not invalidate the four unanimously judged jailbreaks.

assessments.tested_scope: Binary trajectory critic and simple intervention policies across tested HotPotQA/GAIA/ALFWorld agents.
assessments.rationale: Strong offline AUROC coexists with large negative and small positive end-task effects; the p*r-(1-p)*d decomposition and 50-task pilot provide a directly testable decision rule.
limits: Pilot estimates can be noisy and setting-specific.
Results do not cover all recovery mechanisms.
No independent reproduction.

assessments.tested_scope: 2,823 committed episodes, three frameworks/multiple models, telemetry monitor plus deterministic verification and live rollback/rerun.
assessments.rationale: Large multi-setting study reports AUROC/calibration transfer limits and directly measures closed-loop recovery: 45% vs 16% resampling control and task success 52%->73%; code/traces/results released.
limits: Learned monitor requires per-deployment calibration.
Deterministic checks cover only available invariants.
Author artifacts are not independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: SWE-bench Verified early-failure monitoring and same-policy restart with optional interrupted diff.
assessments.rationale: Primary source reports cross-policy monitor transfer, 14.6-20.4% token savings at 5% FPR, and 66.6%->71.8% resolution at 25% FPR versus 66.8% cold restart, directly separating restart carry-forward value.
limits: Current worker artifact had only abstract-level primary verification for richer table details.
Do not infer a universal optimal alarm or cut point.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Checkpoint-restore around irreversible tool effects in the paper's Claude Code/Qwen3-32B bank/cloud/approval testbed.
assessments.rationale: Primary paper identifies two concrete semantic rollback attack classes and validates duplicate-effect/authority-reuse failures, clearly separating semantic equivalence from request-ID idempotency.
limits: Proof-of-concept sample sizes are small.
Full ACRFence defense is proposed rather than implemented/evaluated.
Framework generality is architectural, not empirically exhaustive.

assessments.tested_scope: Atomix prototype under paper workloads/fault injection including append-only external-effect tests and recovery comparisons.
assessments.rationale: Primary work separates task recovery from effect safety; worker source reports 0/500 invalid irreversible leaks with 500/500 valid sends and matched recovery comparisons, supported by public author code.
limits: Prototype is single-process and metadata/adapter-dependent.
Does not establish distributed/full crash-safe exactly-once semantics.
No independent numerical replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Streaming user-revision setting with Idempotent/Reversible/Compensable/Irreversible action taxonomy and Revision Absorber.
assessments.rationale: Formal results make irreversibility/repair cost explicit, and 1,008 StreamBench runs report quality comparable to full restart while discarding 14.6x fewer completed steps.
limits: User-revision setting is not generic failure recovery.
Selector-only historical-target quality remains causally unidentified.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: GAN minimax switching with tested model fixed before fresh evaluation randomness; five-seed CIFAR-10 comparisons.
assessments.rationale: Primary theory directly demonstrates conditional e-process validity inside an adaptive optimization loop and empirical viability across objectives.
limits: Generator-update horizon is matched but discriminator-update compute can differ.
Best-checkpoint IS/FID selection can bias final-quality interpretation.
Transfer to QD/archive mutation is a hypothesis, not theorem.

assessments.tested_scope: Four uncertain-QD tasks, explicit per-generation sampling budget, 10 replications across algorithm/task/sampling-size combinations (1120 runs).
assessments.rationale: Strong matched-budget design directly shows uniform heavy sampling can suppress exploration, while archive/adaptive sampling improves difficult-task corrected QD score and reproducibility; depth D in {1,2,4} is ablated.
limits: D=2 is task-specific, not universal.
Stochastic robotics/QD uncertainty is not LLM-judge class-conditional error.
No direct autonomous-agent population study.

assessments.tested_scope: Official public implementation, corrected Eq.15 Hamming metric, 50 common-random-number paired replicates per selected Figure-4 cell and tau/time sweeps.
assessments.rationale: Paired bootstrap/sign tests robustly localize low-corruption benefit boundaries and an instantaneous-softmax control often matches or beats finite slow routing, materially narrowing mechanistic attribution; official code provenance is direct.
limits: Numerical rerun is worker-local, not independent.
Public code has a metric defect relative to Eq.15 and no fixed released result matrices/seeds.
Does not falsify the paper's separate analytical Lyapunov/fixed-point claims.

assessments.tested_scope: Argus public upstream 962cb06554daaede17b786c495e13ee3; call-path/lock/primitive inspection only.
assessments.rationale: Direct source audit shows normal daemon mutations are serialized by the outer Manager pipeline lock while leaf durable mutators lack authenticated capability and exact state-revision CAS; this precisely narrows the candidate to defense-in-depth.
limits: No current production bypass outside the lock was proven.
No measured reliability/security outcome from adding the proposed capability/CAS.
Filesystem readability is layout-dependent.

assessments.tested_scope: Offline harness-control RL with frozen executor; 20-task held-out adapter evaluations and controlled-domain splits under author scoring.
assessments.rationale: Paper Table 4 plus public code show AW beats BC in all eight settings and Forced CHECK in five, with large gains in coding/tau-bench/DB-Bench and explicit protocol qualification.
limits: Adapter scores are author-defined rather than official benchmark metrics.
Best evidence is for harness control, not formal proving.
Independent replication absent.

assessments.tested_scope: Released training/driver code for the published Advantage Weighting harness policy.
assessments.rationale: Static code trace resolves that return_G is rubric_score_norm and all steps receive a trajectory-level terminal-rubric advantage weight despite richer cost diagnostics being computed elsewhere.
limits: This is implementation provenance, not a separate causal outcome ablation.
Historical paper execution identity still depends on the pinned release matching the reported runs.

assessments.tested_scope: Released epsilon-perturbed collector and legal-action masking/fallback logic.
assessments.rationale: Exact behavior probabilities are derivable from epsilon, legal set and deterministic base action, giving a credible OPE-identifiable collection template.
limits: Ordinary trajectory records do not log epsilon/mask/base policy/full propensities as first-class fields.
Paper does not report an OPE study using these propensities.
Invalid-action fallback/replay identity must be pinned.

assessments.tested_scope: Targeted public-source search over formal-proof agents and outer-loop RL/OPE systems.
assessments.rationale: Search distinguishes tactic-level RL and free-form proof planners from learned heterogeneous outer harness control, keeping a concrete experiment gap.
limits: Absence search is not proof of nonexistence.
No positive quantitative evidence.
Should not be scored as a validated mechanism.

assessments.tested_scope: Six cloud-service categories, 9 production Skills, 98 skill-reference files, four surfaced evolution rounds.
assessments.rationale: Primary abstract verifies +23.0 points over self-reflection and +15.4 over single-turn-QA evolution, directly supporting richer multi-turn feedback as an evolution-gradient source.
limits: Absolute R1-R4 TSR, bloat and regression numbers remain secondary until primary-table verification.
Does not resolve >10-round adaptive promotion validity.
Simulator quality/coverage is a separate failure mode.

assessments.tested_scope: Skill-step Shapley attribution on SkillsBench with boundary-adaptive coalition sampling.
assessments.rationale: Primary abstract supports the mechanism and qualitative ability to identify high/low-value skill steps, but the 99-configuration/206-edge and removal-curve details in the worker artifact were secondary rather than primary-verified.
limits: No primary numeric table verification in this wave.
Fixed-skill Shapley does not establish cross-version causal lineage.
Coupled necessary steps can receive high value without being independently improvable.

assessments.tested_scope: MindMemOS/MindSkillEvolve SpreadsheetBench result plus pinned public online evolve path.
assessments.rationale: Primary abstract verifies +9.2 pp SpreadsheetBench improvement; public code inspection shows trajectory batches can mint/stage evolved skill versions directly into subsequent batches, separating observed online evolution from a held-out acceptance-gate claim.
limits: No independent reproduction.
Public path does not prove paper experiment used no additional hidden validation/checkpoint selection.
Memory-schema validation semantics must not be transferred to skill evolution by name similarity.

source_coverage.scientist_agents_note: The selected scientist_agents artifact is a delta that refines SAGE artifact/recovery boundaries and candidate-027 closure uncertainty but does not introduce a new source-qualified candidate in this exact artifact; no synthetic extra candidate was invented.

material_high_strength: FE-058 is the strongest new benchmark-validity result: a causal multi-model intervention with multi-seed support and released artifacts shows evaluation-design meta-knowledge can inflate apparent safety while increasing benign over-refusal.

Closed-loop long-horizon evidence is strongest where final outcomes are measured, especially Real-Time Detection and Repair, FailFast-RestartSmart, and Atomix; detector quality, restart/carry-forward, and external-effect safety remain separate axes.
Uncertain-QD C49 is unusually strong for resource allocation because reevaluation is explicitly charged against the same sampling budget and archive depth is ablated.
Reasoning C73 has direct paper+code evidence across eight harness-control settings and materially separates learned strategy selection from Forced CHECK process heuristics.
material_holds_or_scope_corrections: No source-matched reproducibility artifact in the frozen snapshot satisfies the current bootstrap_valid contract, so author-code/independent-replication grades are not upgraded from those audits in this C10 artifact.

The valid restore-target audit confirms a high-value negative boundary: current rollback studies do not isolate historical target selection while fixing alarm, candidate set, carry-forward, model, tasks and budget.
Evaluation projection and McNemar-adaptivity entries are rigorous worker-local derivations/simulations, not independent published matched-pair results.
SkillEvo and SkillShapley detailed round/configuration numbers remain secondary until primary full-table verification; only primary-abstract claims are credited.
Argus normal daemon mutation paths are serialized by the existing outer lock; the remaining primitive-bound capability/CAS candidate is defense-in-depth, not a demonstrated normal-path race.
